Thank you for the feedback and the sandbox link. Leveraging the use hook's
implementation to allow React.lazy to read resolved values synchronously is
an interesting suggestion.

I agree that special-casing fallback={null} could introduce subtle
complexity and might not be as robust as a unified approach to how React
handles resolved promises. Exploring whether we can align these internal
implementations to avoid the unnecessary microtask and subsequent throttle
seems like a worthwhile direction.

What do others think about merging the logic between use and React.lazy to
address this?



On Fri, Jun 19, 2026, 4:05 PM MaxwellCohen ***@***.***> wrote:

> *MaxwellCohen* left a comment (react/react#36569)
> <https://github.com/react/react/issues/36569#issuecomment-4754699834>
>
> I think this is an issue with Rect.lazy internal implementation compared
> to use implementation is diffrent. When use has a resolved promise the
> first time, Suspense does not wait 300ms to see the console logs in this
> sandbox <https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/dcjmsz>.
>
> I wonder if there is a way to combine the internal implementations of use
> and Rect.lazy to leverage subclass promises, allowing React to read the
> value synchronously without waiting on a microtask and reducing some
> simi-duplicative code.
>
> Special casing <Suspense fallback={null}> vs <Suspense
> fallback={undefined}> or <Suspense> seems like something that would be
> hard to learn or create bugs.
>
